title: Tommy Dorsey quits and Bill Rank replaces him
summary: Tommy decided to leave in Chicago; Challis recruited Bill Rank, and Tommy impressed the band playing Louis Armstrong choruses on a small trumpet.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: It turned out good and so did the other record, the Washboard and that and I was off to a good start, so in the meantime I'm working out a couple arrangements with like Tommy and Jimmy, trying to get them set in what they like to do. One night out in Chicago, we played three different theatres in Chicago and one night uptown, or downtown, I don't know what it was. It was near the outside of the city, Tommy comes down and says, 'I'm going to quit.' 'What? Gee, we're just getting started. What are you going to do?'
He didn't want to stay in the band. I didn't know whether he had an argument with anybody or what, but --
Were he and Jimmy fighting with each other then?

No more than usual. They didn't room together. I was rooming with Jimmy, but Jimmy came around and said, 'The brother's going to quit.' That's the way they talked about each other. Tommy called Jimmy 'lad.' 'Hey, lad,' and he was younger.
For some reason, I remember growing up and not knowing their ages, I always thought Tommy was the older brother.
He was the younger brother. Jimmy was older.

It's just like the band. He had the band, and he knew what he was going to do with it, he made it, he dumped the -- wholesale dumping out of his band, when he wanted to change it. When a guy on the payroll got too big, this is Tommy -- this is the way a band should be operated, you might say. This guy knows where he's going and knows what he's going to do.

So and the same thing with their lives, Jimmy was an easygoing guy. So he said to me, one time, 'The brother's going to quit and I can't talk him out of it.' 'Well, what are you going to do?' So then I got a call from Whiteman, says Tommy wants to quit. He's going to quit. He said, 'Who do you
think I can get in his place? " I don't know. We had a good trombone player in the Goldkette band, Bill Rank, fine, Good, can you get him? " Oh, I think so .

Anyway it was from Chicago I came back to New York and I went up to the Strand where Bill Rank was playing with Shilkret Childrick (phonetic) and I went in and talked to him and he was tickled to death. Oh, yeah, he'd go. So he joined the band then, someplace on the road. Tommy played for a couple of places after that and Tommy was great. He had a little E-flat -- I think E-flat or C-trumpet about that big, that he used to go around playing all kinds of Louis's choruses. He had every one of them memorized, and he would play them all, besides playing his records, backstage, he'd get this little thing out and play it.
The guys used to like to hear him.
I guess he recorded some on trumpet, in those days, he recorded some dates.
He could have done that, I think, had he stayed in the band a little while --
He would have started to play his trumpet.
